subject: physics
question_text: Give the equation for the value of g at a depth d below the surface of the earth. What is the value of g at the centre of the earth?

verification.note: The mark split is invented and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. The question itself is sourced, not invented.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.why: Only the sphere BELOW your feet pulls you down; the shell above you pulls equally in every direction and cancels.
common_mistakes: Using the height formula g(1 − 2h/R) for depth as well; the depth formula has no factor 2.

recall.must_convey: That g at a depth d is g into one minus d by R.
accept: g into one minus d by R
g d equals g times one minus d over R
reject: g is zero at the centre

lines: At the centre of the earth the depth d equals

lines.text: g = 0 at the centre of the earth

steps.why: At the centre there is no sphere left below you, so there is nothing to pull you — the mass all around cancels.
common_mistakes: Saying g is largest at the centre because that is where the earth’s mass is concentrated.

recall.must_convey: That at the centre d equals R, so g is zero.
accept: g is zero at the centre
d equals R so it vanishes
reject: g into one minus d by R
